precepts.text: Eglon's servants saw the doors of the parlour locked and said, Surely he covereth his feet in his summer chamber, and tarried till they were ashamed; covering the feet is the scripture's phrase for relieving yourself.
precepts.point: Saul went into the cave to cover his feet: that means he was in there relieving himself. See the vulnerable position Saul was in, and yet David spared his life; that is why David could say, thou wast delivered into my hand, but I did not take thy life.

note.label: 1 Samuel 24: David Spares Saul in the Cave at Engedi

precepts.why:
When Eglon's servants came and found “the doors of the parlour were locked, they said, Surely he covereth his feet in his summer chamber. And they tarried till they were ashamed.” Covering the feet is the scripture's phrase for relieving yourself.

So when “Saul went in to cover his feet”, he was in that cave relieving himself. Coming out of the prior chapters, Saul was hunting after David to kill him: he “took three thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and went to seek David and his men upon the rocks of the wild goats”, while “David and his men remained in the sides of the cave.”

See the vulnerable position Saul was in, and yet David spared his life. That is why David could say, thou wast delivered into my hand, but I did not take thy life.

The word skirt in the KJV usually refers to an article of male, not female, clothing, with meanings of extremity and corner. Where we have our fringes attached to the borders of our garments, that is the bottom part of Saul's robe that David cut off privily.

precepts.why:
Ruth said to Boaz, “spread therefore thy skirt over thine handmaid; for thou art a near kinsman.” That is the dictionary's own example of the skirt. The Zondervan Compact Bible Dictionary (page 136) shows the basic garments in general use among men of biblical times were the inner tunic, the tunic coat, the girdle and the cloak, with the headdress and sandals. The word skirt in the KJV usually refers to an article of male, not female, clothing, with meanings of extremity and corner. The skirt is the extremity of the garment.

Where we have our fringes attached to the borders of our garments, that is the bottom part of Saul's robe that David “cut off” “privily.”

And even for that, “David’s heart smote him, because he had cut off Saul’s skirt. And he said unto his men, The Lord forbid that I should do this thing unto my master, the Lord’s anointed.” His men had said, “Behold, I will deliver thine enemy into thine hand.” Who is being referred to as the enemy? His own people: Saul was of the tribe of Benjamin, and David was of the tribe of Judah. “So David stayed his servants with these words, and suffered them not to rise against Saul.”

So the skirt of Saul's robe was its hem and border, the extremity and corner, where we have our fringes attached to the borders of our garments. That bottom part is what David “cut off” “privily.”

precepts.why:
“Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in judgment.” That is what Saul was acknowledging: that David was operating in righteousness.

“Saul lifted up his voice, and wept. And he said to David, Thou art more righteous than I: for thou hast rewarded me good, whereas I have rewarded thee evil.” “For if a man find his enemy, will he let him go well away?”

Saul saw the righteousness of David, and so he said, “I know well that thou shalt surely be king, and that the kingdom of Israel shall be established in thine hand.”

precepts.point: David showed this with Saul: he cut off the skirt of Saul's robe in the cave but would not kill the Most High's anointed, and Saul confessed David was more righteous, rewarding good for evil. The coals of fire are the shame that comes on such an enemy.

note.label: Proverbs 25: The Proverbs of Solomon Copied by Hezekiah's Men

precepts.why:
David showed what it is to do good to an enemy among your own people. Saul was hunting him, and “he came to the sheepcotes by the way, where was a cave; and Saul went in to cover his feet: and David and his men remained in the sides of the cave.” His men told him, “Behold the day of which the Lord said unto thee, Behold, I will deliver thine enemy into thine hand, that thou mayest do to him as it shall seem good unto thee.”

David had Saul in his hand. “Then David arose, and cut off the skirt of Saul’s robe privily.” He cut off the skirt of Saul's robe in the cave, but would not kill the Most High's anointed.

That is bread for the hungry enemy: the enemy in your hand, and you spare him. And the coals of fire on his head are the shame that comes on such an enemy when he learns what you could have done and did not.

precepts.text: Saul wept and said David was more righteous, for David rewarded him good where Saul rewarded evil.
precepts.point: David showed this with Saul: he cut off the skirt of Saul's robe in the cave but would not kill the Most High's anointed, and Saul confessed David was more righteous, rewarding good for evil. The coals of fire are the shame that comes on such an enemy.

note.label: Proverbs 25: The Proverbs of Solomon Copied by Hezekiah's Men

precepts.why:
After David spared him in the cave, “Saul said, Is this thy voice, my son David? And Saul lifted up his voice, and wept. And he said to David, Thou art more righteous than I: for thou hast rewarded me good, whereas I have rewarded thee evil.”

Saul wept and confessed David was more righteous, rewarding good for evil. Those are the coals of fire heaped on the enemy's head: the shame that comes on such an enemy when good is returned for his evil.

“For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord shall reward thee.” David gave good to an enemy among his own people, Saul was put to shame by it, and the Lord rewarded David. That is the proverb lived out.

precepts.text: Thou art more righteous than I: for thou hast rewarded me good, whereas I have rewarded thee evil.
precepts.point: The reason for the command is that the enemy may yet repent, as one who persecuted the disciples afterward became one of them.

note.label: Matthew 5: The Sermon on the Mount and the Magnifying of the Law

precepts.why:
David did good to Saul when he could have killed him, and Saul had to confess it: “Thou art more righteous than I: for thou hast rewarded me good, whereas I have rewarded thee evil.”

This is loving your enemy and doing good to them that hate you, lived out between two Israelites. The reason for the command is that the enemy may yet repent, as one who persecuted the disciples afterward became one of them. Saul's own mouth acknowledged David's righteousness because David rewarded good for evil.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: And he came to the sheepcotes by the way, where was a cave; and Saul went in to cover his feet: and David and his men remained in the sides of the cave.
So when you read about David killing thousands at a time, look. The Lord made his feet like hinds' feet. He was able to leap over walls. David was not a regular dude with a beer belly and bad feet.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: And the men of David said unto him, Behold the day of which the Lord said unto thee, Behold, I will deliver thine enemy into thine hand, that thou mayest do to him as it shall seem good unto thee. Then David arose, and cut off the skirt of Saul's robe privily.

So think about this. The mighty men that are with David said, hey, this is the day the Lord has been telling you about. He is going to deliver your enemies into your hand. So imagine, they are in a cave. Saul is covering his feet, meaning he is doing what? Just like your trousers go down to your ankle, they cover your feet. Saul is by himself in the cave. The king does not sleep by himself. When you read about King Solomon, he had sixty men around his bed. But you are going to do a number two by yourself.

David and his men are in the cave and they see King Saul. I want you to think about how stealthily David has to move to perform the next act, in a cave where King Saul does not realize he is even there, his men are even there. These are mighty men. He was able to get close enough to Saul to cut off a piece of his robe without King Saul realizing he was there.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: And he said to David, Thou art more righteous than I: for thou hast rewarded me good, whereas I have rewarded thee evil. What did King Saul say? When David showed him, hey Saul, I have got a piece of your coat. Saul looks and checks, sees where David cut it off privily, and he was not even aware. Meaning David could have killed him. So now Saul says, thou art more righteous than I. Because if the shoe was on the other foot, Saul would have killed David.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: And thou hast shewed this day how that thou hast dealt well with me: forasmuch as when the Lord had delivered me into thine hand, thou killedst me not. So Saul acknowledges that David is more righteous than him.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: These men were warriors. These men could fight; these men were swordsmen. If they wanted to, they could have subdued Saul and his men. But no, King David said, no, I'm going to take the bigger position. He was chosen before me. Yes, he's becoming obsolete, but still David showed respect unto King Saul.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

That's the same spirit that's in King David, and that's the same spirit we got to have. We got to make sure that hatred don't spread on us.

points: You ever seen Fallen with Denzel? If you get a chance, watch it. Remember that evil spirit that was going around and inhabiting the men and causing them to commit murder, anger, and all that evil? It's the same thing. We got to make sure that evil spirit don't jump on us. We're not going to go tit for tat. We're not going to slander. Yeah, we're going to call you out like we doing now in this class; we're going to shine a light on your wicked behind. But we're not going to make these stupid videos. We're not going to get physical with brothers, only if it's for self-defense. The house of David is not going to become like the house of Saul. And the house of David is in IUIC.
